name: AMQP
description: AMQP (Advanced Message Queuing Protocol) is a message-queuing protocol for reliably routing messages between producers and consumers, used by brokers such as RabbitMQ. Port 5672 is its IANA-registered default.

name: Angular
description: Angular is a TypeScript-based frontend framework maintained by Google. Its CLI's development server defaults to port 4200, a value set by the framework's own convention.

name: Astro
description: Astro is a frontend framework focused on shipping mostly static, content-driven sites with minimal client-side JavaScript. Its dev server defaults to port 4321, a playful rocket-countdown nod chosen by the project.

name: BGP
description: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) is the routing protocol that exchanges reachability information between autonomous systems on the Internet. It is the protocol that decides how traffic crosses between ISPs.

name: chargen
description: Character Generator (chargen) sends a continuous stream of test characters to any client that connects, historically used to test network throughput. It is now mostly disabled, since it has been abused to amplify UDP denial-of-service attacks.

name: Consul
description: Consul is a service networking tool from HashiCorp providing service discovery, health checking, and a key-value store. Its HTTP API and web UI default to port 8500.

name: Create React App
description: Create React App was Meta's official, zero-config tool for scaffolding a React project, running a development server that defaulted to port 3000. The React team formally deprecated it in February 2025 in favor of tools like Vite.

name: Daytime
description: The Daytime protocol returns the current date and time as human-readable text when a client connects, a simple predecessor to NTP for checking a server's clock.

name: DHCP
description: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) automatically assigns IP addresses and network settings to devices joining a network. Servers listen on port 67 while clients receive replies on port 68.

name: Discard
description: The Discard protocol silently drops any data sent to it, used historically to test outbound connectivity and to generate throwaway network traffic.

name: Django
description: Django is a full-featured Python web framework. Its `runserver` development command defaults to port 8000, a common convention for Python web apps.

name: DNS
description: DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses and other records. It mostly runs over UDP for speed on port 53, falling back to TCP for larger responses such as zone transfers.

name: Docker API
description: The Docker Engine API lets clients and tools manage containers, images, and networks remotely. Port 2375 is its plain, unencrypted convention; Docker recommends port 2376 with TLS for anything beyond local testing.

name: Echo
description: The Echo protocol simply sends back whatever data it receives, historically used to test that a host is reachable and responsive. It predates ICMP ping as a connectivity check.

name: Elasticsearch
description: Elasticsearch is a distributed search and analytics engine. It exposes its REST API on port 9200 by default, with a separate port, 9300, reserved for inter-node cluster communication.

name: Finger
description: Finger returns information about a user on a remote system, such as their login name and last login time. It is rarely run today because it can leak personal and account details to anyone who asks.

name: Flask
description: Flask is a lightweight Python web framework. Its built-in development server defaults to port 5000, which on modern macOS often conflicts with the built-in AirPlay Receiver service.

name: FTP
description: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is a client-server protocol for uploading and downloading files between hosts, using a separate control connection and data connection. It has used port 21 for control commands since the earliest Internet standards.

name: Git
description: The Git protocol is a fast, unauthenticated transport for fetching from a repository served by `git daemon`. Git-over-SSH and Git-over-HTTPS, which add authentication, have largely superseded it.

name: Gopher
description: Gopher is a menu-driven document retrieval protocol that predates the web, organizing content into hierarchical, text-based listings. HTTP and the web largely displaced it during the 1990s.

name: Grafana
description: Grafana is an observability platform for building dashboards from metrics, logs, and traces across many data sources. Its web UI defaults to port 3000, the same default several JavaScript dev servers also use.

name: HTTP
description: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is the request-response protocol that underlies the web, fetching pages, APIs, and other resources. Port 80 has been its default, unencrypted port since the web's earliest days.

name: HTTP-alt
description: HTTP-alt is the common fallback port for web servers and proxies when port 80 is unavailable or reserved, widely used for local development and alternate HTTP services. IANA registers 8080 under the service name "http-alt".

name: HTTPS
description: HTTPS is HTTP carried over a TLS-encrypted connection, protecting requests and responses from eavesdropping and tampering. Port 443 became the default encrypted web port in the mid-1990s and now carries most web traffic.

name: Ident
description: Ident (the Identification Protocol) tells a remote server which local user owns a given TCP connection, historically used by IRC networks and mail servers to log or authenticate connecting users.

name: IMAP
description: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) lets a mail client read and manage messages that stay stored on the server, keeping read state and folders synced across multiple devices.

name: IMAPS
description: IMAPS is IMAP wrapped in implicit TLS from the start of the connection. Port 993 is its dedicated encrypted port, following the implicit-TLS guidance in RFC 8314.

name: IRC
description: IRC (Internet Relay Chat) is a text-based, real-time group chat protocol organized around channels on a server. Port 6667 is its traditional, unencrypted default.

name: iSCSI
description: iSCSI (Internet Small Computer Systems Interface) carries SCSI storage commands over TCP/IP, letting a client mount a remote block device as if it were a local disk.

name: Jenkins
description: Jenkins is an open-source automation server used to build, test, and deploy software through configurable pipelines. Its web UI defaults to port 8080, its long-standing installer default.

name: Kerberos
description: Kerberos is a network authentication protocol that uses tickets issued by a trusted key distribution center, letting users and services prove their identity without sending passwords over the network.

name: Kibana
description: Kibana is the visualization and dashboard front end for Elasticsearch, letting users search, chart, and explore indexed data. Its web UI defaults to port 5601.

name: Kubernetes API
description: The Kubernetes API server is the cluster's control-plane front end, handling every read and write to cluster state. Port 6443 is its conventional secure default across most cluster setups.

name: LDAP
description: LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) queries and modifies directory services such as user and group records. It is the protocol behind most enterprise identity systems, including Active Directory.

name: LDAPS
description: LDAPS is LDAP wrapped in implicit TLS from the start of the connection, rather than upgrading via StartTLS on port 389. Port 636 is its dedicated encrypted directory-service port.

name: MinIO
description: MinIO is a self-hosted object storage server compatible with the Amazon S3 API, commonly used to run S3-style storage on-premises or in development, defaulting to port 9000 for that S3 API. MinIO Inc. discontinued the open-source project in 2026 in favor of its commercial AIStor product.

name: mongo-express
description: mongo-express is a web-based admin UI for browsing and editing MongoDB databases and collections. Its default port, 8081, is set by the project's own configuration.

name: MQTT
description: MQTT is a lightweight publish-subscribe messaging protocol designed for constrained devices and unreliable networks, widely used in IoT. Port 1883 is its IANA-registered, unencrypted default.

name: MySQL
description: MySQL is a relational database. Its server listens on port 3306 for the MySQL client protocol that drivers and command-line tools use to authenticate and run queries.

name: Next.js
description: Next.js is a React framework providing server-side rendering, static generation, and file-based routing. Its development server defaults to port 3000, a default shared by several Node-based frameworks.

name: NFS
description: NFS (Network File System) lets a client mount and use a remote directory as if it were local. Port 2049 has been its main port since early NFS versions; NFS version 4 consolidated its auxiliary services onto that one port too, no longer needing a separate port-mapper service.

name: NTP
description: NTP (Network Time Protocol) synchronizes computer clocks over a network to a common reference time. It is one of the oldest Internet protocols still in wide use, with its design dating to the 1980s.

name: Nuxt
description: Nuxt is a Vue framework offering server-side rendering, static generation, and file-based routing, playing a similar role for Vue that Next.js plays for React. Its dev server also defaults to port 3000.

name: OpenVPN
description: OpenVPN is an open-source VPN protocol and software that tunnels traffic over an encrypted TLS connection. Port 1194 is its IANA-registered default, usually run over UDP.

name: pgAdmin
description: pgAdmin is a web-based administration and query tool for PostgreSQL. The project's official Docker image is commonly published to host port 5050 in its own setup examples, mapped to port 80 inside the container.

name: POP3
description: POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) lets a mail client download messages from a server, typically removing them from the server afterward. IMAP has mostly replaced it because IMAP keeps mail synced across devices.

name: POP3S
description: POP3S is POP3 wrapped in implicit TLS from the start of the connection. Port 995 is its dedicated encrypted port, following the same implicit-TLS guidance as IMAPS and SMTPS.

name: PostgreSQL
description: PostgreSQL is a relational database. Its server listens on port 5432 for the frontend/backend protocol that clients use to authenticate, run queries, and stream results.

name: Prometheus
description: Prometheus is a monitoring system that scrapes and stores time-series metrics from configured targets, with its own query language for alerting and dashboards. Its web UI and API default to port 9090.

name: RabbitMQ UI
description: RabbitMQ's management plugin provides a web UI and HTTP API for monitoring and managing the message broker's queues, exchanges, and connections. It listens on port 15672, separate from the broker's own AMQP port, 5672.

name: RADIUS
description: RADIUS (Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service) centralizes authentication, authorization, and accounting for network access, commonly used by VPNs, Wi-Fi, and switches. Port 1812 replaced an earlier, conflicting port.

name: Rails
description: Ruby on Rails is a full-stack web framework for Ruby. Its built-in server has defaulted to port 3000 since Rails' earliest releases, a default many later frameworks copied.

name: RDP
description: RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) is Microsoft's protocol for graphical remote access to a Windows machine's desktop. It has used port 3389 since Windows NT 4.0 Terminal Server Edition.

name: Redis
description: Redis is an in-memory data store used as a cache, message broker, and fast key-value database. Port 6379 is its IANA-registered default, listed under the service name "redis".

name: Rsync
description: Rsync synchronizes files and directories between systems, transferring only the changed portions of files to minimize bandwidth. Running as a standalone daemon, it listens on port 873.

name: SIP
description: SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) sets up, modifies, and tears down voice, video, and messaging sessions such as VoIP calls. It only handles the signaling; a separate protocol, RTP, carries the actual media.

name: SMB
description: SMB (Server Message Block) shares files, printers, and named pipes between Windows systems and compatible clients such as Samba. Port 445 carries SMB directly over TCP, replacing the older NetBIOS-based ports.

name: SMTP
description: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is the protocol mail servers use to relay email to one another. Port 25 has been its standard server-to-server delivery port since the protocol was defined.

name: SMTPS
description: SMTPS is SMTP wrapped in an implicit TLS connection from the start, rather than upgrading mid-session with STARTTLS. Port 465 was reassigned to this purpose after RFC 8314 recommended implicit TLS for mail.

name: SNMP
description: SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) lets network devices such as routers and switches expose status and configuration data to monitoring tools. Agents listen for queries on port 161, and devices send unsolicited traps on port 162.

name: SSH
description: SSH (Secure Shell) is a protocol for encrypted remote login and command execution between hosts, replacing Telnet for anything security-sensitive. IANA registered it on port 22 in 1995.

name: Storybook
description: Storybook is a tool for building and testing UI components in isolation, outside a full application. Its dev server defaults to port 6006, a value the project chose with no special registry meaning.

name: Submission
description: Message submission is the protocol a mail client uses to hand a new message to its own outgoing server, distinct from server-to-server relay on port 25. It typically requires authentication and STARTTLS on port 587.

name: SvelteKit
description: SvelteKit is the official application framework built on Svelte, handling routing, server rendering, and bundling. Its dev server runs on Vite under the hood, which is why it shares Vite's default port, 5173.
blurb: Full-stack app framework built on Vite

name: Syslog
description: Syslog is a standard for forwarding log messages from devices and applications to a central logging server. Port 514 is its traditional UDP port, though many deployments now use TLS on other ports for reliability and security.

name: Telnet
description: Telnet is a protocol for interactive, text-based remote terminal sessions over a network. It sends all traffic, including passwords, in plain text, which is why SSH has replaced it for anything security-sensitive.

name: TFTP
description: TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol) is a stripped-down file transfer protocol with no login or directory listing, commonly used to boot diskless devices and network hardware over UDP.

name: Tomcat
description: Apache Tomcat is a Java servlet container that runs Java web applications and JSPs. It has shipped with port 8080 as its default HTTP connector since its earliest releases.

name: Vault
description: Vault is HashiCorp's tool for securely storing and controlling access to secrets such as API keys, passwords, and certificates. Its API defaults to port 8200.

name: Vite
description: Vite is a frontend build tool and development server that serves modules over native ES imports during development and bundles with Rollup for production. Its dev server defaults to port 5173.

name: VNC
description: VNC (Virtual Network Computing) shares a remote desktop's screen and input over the RFB protocol. Its first display listens on port 5900, with each additional display adding one to the port number.

name: webpack-dev-server
description: webpack-dev-server serves a webpack-bundled application and reloads it in the browser as source files change during development. It defaults to port 8080, one of the most common alternate HTTP ports.

name: WHOIS
description: WHOIS looks up registration information for a domain name or IP address block, such as its owner and registrar. It is a simple text query-response protocol with no built-in authentication.

name: WireGuard
description: WireGuard is a modern VPN protocol built around a small codebase and current cryptography, tunneling traffic over UDP. Port 51820 is its conventional default, though it is not a formally registered IANA port.
